Advanced knowledge and experience working in an academic, health or health sciences setting. Advanced knowledge of the principles of higher education and of an academic institution's organization, structure, and function.

Demonstrated advanced experience providing high-level management support and advice to high level academic Executives, preferably in an academic medical center, on a wide range of issues associated with complex problems of a highly confidential and extremely sensitive nature.

Demonstrated advanced experience serving as a primary liaison for a senior executive in an academic institution, interfacing with senior leaders as well as all levels of personnel. Demonstrated advanced experience serving as representative for an executive in regards to interactions with the community, VIP/donors, and campus-related meetings/briefing/committees.
Demonstrated experience and proven ability to function at a high administrative level and represent the University's best interests at all times.

The University of California San Diego (UC San Diego) School of Medicine (SOM) is dedicated to serving its communities and creating a healthier world by being the preeminent destination for transformative, innovative, and impactful research, medical education, and clinical care.As the only medical school in the region and the largest school at UC San Diego, SOM is home to more than 1,800 faculty, 1,000 medical and graduate students, and over 1,000 residents and post-doctoral fellows across 20 academic departments. SOM is housed within UC San Diego Health Sciences, which comprises three professional schools, more than 30 research institutes, and a growing clinical practice at UC San Diego Health—the top-ranked health system in the region.In fiscal year 2025, the School of Medicine secured nearly $654 million in research awards, accounting for 78% of research funding within Health Sciences.

The Office of the Dean is responsible for leading SOM’s overall strategic vision; developing and implementing initiatives that enhance teaching, research, and clinical care across its departments, the Division of Medical Education and Division of Graduate Education; and establishing collaborative partnerships across campus and the community to advance its mission.The Executive Assistant to the Dean provides high-level executive support to the Dean of the School of Medicine and serves as a key member of the Dean's Office Administrative Core. Reporting to the Chief of Staff, the incumbent works independently to manage the administrative operations that support the Dean's leadership of the School of Medicine and ensures the effective coordination of executive priorities, communications, and activities.

The position serves as a primary point of contact for the Dean and regularly interacts with senior university and health system leaders, department chairs, faculty, staff, donors, and external stakeholders. The incumbent handles highly sensitive and confidential matters requiring discretion, sound judgment, diplomacy, and professionalism.

The Executive Assistant manages the Dean's complex calendar and schedule; coordinates meetings, events, travel, and special engagements; prepares briefing materials and correspondence; and ensures appropriate follow-through on priorities and commitments. The incumbent facilitates communication and coordination among School of Medicine departments, UC San Diego Health, Health Sciences leadership, campus partners, and external organizations; supports leadership recruitment activities, governance and advisory committees, and special projects led by the Dean and Chief of Staff; and contributes to the efficient operation of the Dean's Office through continuous process improvement and implementation of administrative best practices.
Political acumen and sensitivities to the differing perspectives and political circumstances within all levels of the organization as well as the Office of the President and external constituencies.

Strong analytical / problem-solving skills. Strong skills to analyze quickly and produce results/synopses of professional documents of high caliber.

Strong skills to communicate and influence effectively with all levels of staff, faculty, alumni / donors, students and external constituents, both verbally and in writing. Strong skills to communicate clearly and effectively in person, on the phone and in writing. Superior English grammar and spelling skills.
Knowledge of biomedical education systems and graduate medical education.
Advising and counseling skills.
Proven ability to focus on key issues with an understanding of the broad range of issues facing a senior administrator in an academic medical center environment.
